sheets.name: README
rows: Traceability view for one regulation-to-SHACL generation run.
Generation is frozen before RDF execution; no ship graph or hidden expected outcome is used here.
events.jsonl is append-only; CSV and Excel sheets are derived views.
Static validation passed and the semantic validator accepted the candidate.
No verified canonical term was available; the generator was not allowed to invent one.
Accepted shapes await the separate bulk evaluator.

sheets.name: RUNS
rows: Reverse the conditional draught comparison: because draught increases downward, the summer load line is at a higher level than the UIWL when ?summerValue < ?uiwlValue, not when it is greater. Change the SPARQL target filter to FILTER (?summerValue < ?uiwlValue); no vocabulary lookup is needed.

sheets.name: ITERATIONS
rows: Repair the evidence boundaries and accidental-pass logic. Validate retainedOnBoard and readilyAvailableToMaster on the node reached by hasIceDraughtRestrictionDocument, and validate all six maximum/minimum draught values on the node reached by hasClassCertificate; the current independent ship-level facts do not establish that the restrictions are kept with the document or that the draughts are indicated in the certificate. Compare the amidships mark against the certificate’s maximumIceClassDraughtAmidships value. Refactor the large disjunctive SPARQL constraint: use SHACL Core nested shapes for documents, certificates, booleans, and the pre-/post-2007 date alternatives, an applicability target for summerLoadLineFreshWaterDraught > upperIceWaterlineDraught, and only one bounded SPARQL constraint for the tolerant mark-value comparison. For pre-1-July-2007 ships require firstScheduledDryDockingDate > 2007-07-01; for ships built on or after that date use the immediate marking branch. Add maxCount 1 where these dates, booleans, quantities, numeric values, and units are scalar, otherwise one conforming value or mark/maximum pair can hide conflicting values.

The graph omits the required iceClass applicability operand and consequently applies the document/certificate duties to every nltl:ship while applying the marking rule to every ship having the draught comparison. Retarget the requirement shapes to ships whose nltl:iceClass is one of the supplied Finnish-Swedish ice-class controlled values, and include that condition in the marking target. For those applicable ships, require exactly one summerLoadLineFreshWaterDraught and upperIceWaterlineDraught (valid metre QuantityValues) so missing comparison operands cannot silently avoid the conditional marking check.

Reverse the conditional draught comparison: because draught increases downward, the summer load line is at a higher level than the UIWL when ?summerValue < ?uiwlValue, not when it is greater. Change the SPARQL target filter to FILTER (?summerValue < ?uiwlValue); no vocabulary lookup is needed.
